The LV welcome the KC as underdogs of 5.5, with the total set at 43.5 — a market that implies a KC 24–19 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 40% of its snaps with KC in front, 36% within one score, and 24% with KC chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

A modest edge to KC. They should lead more often than not, tilting them slightly toward the run late, while LV leans a touch more pass-heavy to stay in it — but the effect is gentle; this isn't a script that dramatically reshapes anyone's usage.

The Key Matchups

Patrick Mahomes adds rushing value — he scrambles on 4.8% of dropbacks, live for rush-yard and anytime-TD props.

Tough sledding for Ashton Jeanty — KC are stingy against the run (108 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

Tre Tucker faces a tough cover — KC hold WR1s to just 50 yds/game (vs ~58); a rec-yards under lean.

Touchdown Board

Travis Kelce is a live anytime-TD dart — LV are leaky to tight ends in the end zone (0.32 TE TDs/game vs ~0.24).

Rashee Rice carries TD equity — LV surrender 0.44 WR1 receiving scores a game.

In the red zone KC throw it (56% pass inside the 20) — Rashee Rice's TD equity over a goal-line back.

In the red zone LV throw it (59% pass inside the 20) — Tre Tucker's TD equity over a goal-line back.

Game Script, Pace & Environment

A modest lean to KC — they should lead more often than not, nudging them toward the run late and giving Kenneth Walker III a gentle game-script tailwind.

Indoors — a dome removes weather variance and historically nudges passing efficiency up; a small tailwind for the passing games.

KC — a pass-heavy offense

KC stay aggressive through the air even with a lead — they pass 50% on early downs when ahead versus the league's 44%. They don't sit on the ball, which keeps their receivers live in scripts where most offenses would be running out the clock.

Kenneth Walker III (15 carries, 65 yards projected) gets a mild game-script tailwind as a favorite, though KC's willingness to keep throwing when ahead caps how much the lead converts into extra carries.

Rashee Rice projects for 9 targets and 77 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Travis Kelce (TE, 6 targets, 51 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

LV — a balanced offense

LV are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (46% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

Game script works against the run here — LV project to trail and throw, which squeezes Ashton Jeanty's rushing projection (17 carries, 64 yards) but raises his value as a receiver; trailing teams check the ball down, and his target share ticks up as the game gets away from them.

Tre Tucker is the one to target from a volume standpoint: as underdogs throwing to keep pace, LV funnel work to their top receiver — 6 targets for 44 yards projected, with genuine upside if they fall behind early and the game turns one-dimensional.

Underneath, Brock Bowers (TE, 6 targets, 49 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 6-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.

This preview and the projections below regenerate through the week as injuries, weather and line moves update the inputs.
